Today Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 1, completely skipping 27.1 in the testing cycle. Among other changes, the new iOS 27.2 update also includes the newly announced "Health" app.

Brand new Apple "Health" app debuts in iOS 27.2 beta 1

At last week's September event, Apple announced a brand new "Health" app that will arrive on iPhone later this year.

And today, beta testers got an early look at this redesigned "Health" app through iOS 27.2 beta 1.

When Apple first introduced the new "Health" app, it emphasised how it uses Apple Intelligence to help users better understand their own health. Here's what Apple said:

And in today's iOS 27.2 beta 1, if you're a developer, you can try out the new "Insights" tab and "Longevity" tab.

Since the new "Health" app relies on Apple Intelligence, you'll need an AI-capable iPhone to try it out. Some features also require pairing with an Apple Watch, and your device language must be set to US English.

So, if your iPhone isn't as powerful as the iPhone 15 Pro, or you don't have a compatible Apple Watch, you won't be able to access the upgraded features of the "Health" app. But for other users, iOS 27.2 offers a window to get an early look at Apple's expanded vision for the "Health" app.

Note: Apple says more "Health" features will roll out in subsequent betas, such as booking lab tests through Quest, as well as personalised recommendations. Additionally, although the new "Health" app is available in the beta, Apple says it won't launch officially with iOS 27.2, but will arrive later this year.

What do you think of the changes to the "Health" app in iOS 27.2? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
